p.src: Now Jia Zheng was holding a banquet there when Lai Da suddenly hurried into the Hall of Glorious Felicity and reported, “Lord Zhao, the chief officer of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, has come with several departmental officials and says he wishes to pay his respects. I asked for his calling card so that I might announce him, but Lord Zhao said, ‘We are intimate friends; there is no need.’ He then alighted from his carriage and came straight in. Master, please go quickly with the other gentlemen to receive him.” Hearing this, Jia Zheng thought, “Lord Zhao has never had any dealings with me. Why has he come? I have guests here now; it would be awkward to ask him to stay, yet discourteous not to.” While he was still deliberating, Jia Lian said, “Uncle, hurry and go. If you think any longer, they will already be inside.” Even as he spoke, a servant from the second gate came in to report, “Lord Zhao has already passed the second gate.” Jia Zheng and the others hastened out to receive him. They saw Chief Officer Zhao, his face all smiles, say nothing at all but proceed directly into the hall. Five or six departmental officials followed behind him, some familiar and others unknown, but none of them answered a word. Jia Zheng and the others could make nothing of it and could only follow them in and offer them seats. Some of the assembled relatives and friends knew Chief Officer Zhao. Seeing him hold his head high and scarcely acknowledge anyone, while merely taking Jia Zheng by the hand and smiling through a few conventional greetings, they grew uneasy. Realizing that his visit boded ill, some slipped into the inner rooms while others stood waiting respectfully with hands lowered. Just as Jia Zheng was about to begin a smiling conversation, a servant reported in alarm, “His Highness the Prince of Xiping has arrived.” Jia Zheng hurried out to receive him, but the prince was already entering. Chief Officer Zhao rushed forward to pay his respects, then said, “Now that Your Highness has arrived, the gentlemen who accompanied you should lead the yamen runners to guard the front and rear gates.” The officials assented and went out. Jia Zheng and the others knew that something was amiss and hurriedly knelt to receive the prince. The Prince of Xiping raised them with both hands and said with a genial smile, “I would not presume to intrude without cause. I have been entrusted by imperial command with a matter, and Master She must receive the decree. The banquet in this hall is not yet over, and I imagine it would be inconvenient with relatives and friends present. Let all your guests disperse, and only members of this household remain to await orders.” Chief Officer Zhao replied, “Your Highness is merciful, but as for the affair at the eastern mansion, the prince in charge conducts business rigorously; I expect its gates have already been sealed.” The company realized that both mansions were implicated and longed desperately to escape. The prince smiled and said, “Please, gentlemen, go freely. Have someone escort them out for me and tell the officers of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard that they are all relatives and friends. They need not be questioned; let them out at once.” At these words, the relatives and friends fled as swiftly as smoke before the wind. Only Jia She, Jia Zheng, and the rest remained, their faces ashen with terror and their bodies trembling all over. Before long, countless constables poured in and took guard at every gate. No one in the household, high or low, was permitted to take a single step without authorization.

p.src: Chief Officer Zhao's expression abruptly changed as he turned to the prince and said, “Your Highness, please proclaim the decree so that we may begin.” The constables tucked up their robes and bared their arms, waiting only for the order. The Prince of Xiping said slowly, “By imperial command, I have brought Zhao Quan of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard to inspect Jia She's property.” On hearing this, Jia She and the others prostrated themselves on the floor. The prince stood above them and announced, “Here is the imperial decree: ‘Jia She has colluded with provincial officials and relied upon his power to oppress the weak. He has betrayed Our favor and brought disgrace upon the virtue of his ancestors. His hereditary rank is hereby revoked. Respect this.’” Chief Officer Zhao shouted repeatedly, “Seize Jia She! Keep all the others under guard!” At that time Jia She, Jia Zheng, Jia Lian, Jia Zhen, Jia Rong, Jia Qiang, Jia Zhi, and Jia Lan were all present. Only Baoyu, pretending to be ill, was making a commotion in Grandmother Jia's quarters, while Jia Huan seldom appeared before company in any case. The men who were present were therefore placed under guard. Chief Officer Zhao immediately ordered one of his attendants, “Summon all the departmental officials. Have them take the constables and search the rooms separately, entering everything in the register.” At this order, Jia Zheng and everyone in the household stared at one another in terror, while the delighted constables and attendants rubbed their fists and palms, eager to begin ransacking every quarter. The Prince of Xiping said, “I understand that Master She and Master Zheng live in separate quarters and maintain separate kitchens. In obedience to the decree, we should inspect Jia She's property. For the present, seal the other rooms; after we report to the throne, we shall await a further decision.” Chief Officer Zhao rose and said, “Your Highness, Jia She and Jia Zheng have not divided the family estate. I hear that their nephew Jia Lian is now in overall charge of the household; therefore, we cannot refrain from confiscating everything.” The Prince of Xiping heard him but said nothing. Chief Officer Zhao continued, “I had better personally lead the searches of Jia Lian's and Jia She's quarters.” The Prince of Xiping replied, “There is no need to hurry. First send word to the inner apartments and ask the women to withdraw. It will not be too late to search afterward.” Before he had finished speaking, old Zhao's attendants and constables had already seized servants of the household to guide them and gone off in separate parties to search and confiscate. The prince shouted, “No disorderly clamor! Wait until I inspect the premises myself.” With that, he slowly rose as if to leave and ordered, “Not one of my attendants is to move. All of you remain standing here. When I return, we shall witness the registration together.” As he spoke, an officer of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard knelt and reported, “Inside we have found robes and skirts reserved for imperial use, as well as a number of prohibited articles. We dared not touch them without authority and have returned to seek Your Highness's instructions.” A short while later, another party came and stopped the prince to report, “In the eastern side quarters we found two chests of title deeds to houses and land, and another chest of promissory notes, all bearing interest charged in violation of the regulations.” Old Zhao exclaimed, “What ruthless usury! Everything certainly ought to be confiscated! Your Highness, please remain seated here and let me go confiscate it all; then we can await your decision.”

p.src: Just then, the Prince of Beijing reached the great hall. Standing there facing outward, he proclaimed, “An imperial decree! Zhao Quan of the Imperial Guard Office, attend and hear it.” He continued, “By imperial command: ‘The officers of the Imperial Guard are to take only Jia She into custody for interrogation; all other matters are entrusted to the Prince of Xiping, who shall investigate and dispose of them in accordance with this decree. Respect this.’” The Prince of Xiping received the decree with immense relief. He sat down with the Prince of Beijing and ordered Zhao, the presiding officer, to take Jia She back to his office. When the men conducting the search inside heard that the Prince of Beijing had arrived, they all came out together. On learning that Officer Zhao was leaving, they were thoroughly crestfallen and could only stand by awaiting orders. The Prince of Beijing selected two honest departmental officials and some ten elderly constables, then expelled all the rest. The Prince of Xiping said, “I was just losing my temper with old Zhao. Fortunately, Your Highness arrived with the decree; otherwise this household would have suffered grievously.” The Prince of Beijing replied, “When I heard at court that Your Highness had been commanded to search the Jia residence, my mind was quite at ease, for I trusted that no cruelty would be inflicted here. I never imagined old Zhao would behave so outrageously. But where are Master Zheng and Baoyu now? And how far has the turmoil inside gone?” The attendants reported, “Jia Zheng and the others are being held under guard in the servants’ quarters. Inside, the search has already thrown everything into utter confusion.” The Prince of Xiping ordered the officials, “Bring Jia Zheng here at once for questioning.” They ordered that he be brought forward. Jia Zheng knelt to pay his respects and, unable to restrain his tears, begged for mercy. The Prince of Beijing rose and took him by the arm, saying, “Master Zheng, set your mind at rest.” He then told him the contents of the decree. Jia Zheng wept with gratitude, faced north and again gave thanks for the imperial grace, then came forward once more to await instructions. The prince said, “Master Zheng, while old Zhao was here just now, the constables reported finding prohibited articles and promissory notes for loans at extortionate interest. We cannot very well conceal those matters. The prohibited articles were originally procured for presentation to the Imperial Consort; if we make that clear, they will cause no difficulty. It is only the loan bonds for which we must devise some remedy. For now, Master Zheng, accompany the officials and truthfully surrender all of Master She’s property. That will settle the affair. You must on no account conceal anything further and thereby incur guilt yourself.” Jia Zheng replied, “This guilty official would never dare do so again. However, the estate left by my forefathers has never been divided; only the possessions in the houses occupied by each family member have been regarded as that person’s own.” The two princes replied, “That presents no difficulty. You need only surrender everything belonging to Master She’s side of the household.” They further ordered the officials to carry out their instructions and forbade them to meddle or move things recklessly. The officials received their orders and departed.

p.src: Meanwhile, the ladies on Grandmother Jia’s side were also holding a family banquet. Lady Wang was saying, “If Baoyu does not go out front, I fear his father will be angry.” Xifeng, moaning and groaning with illness, said, “I do not think Baoyu is afraid of anyone. He sees that there are already plenty of people entertaining the guests out front, so perhaps he has stayed here to look after things. If the master should remember that no one is here to attend to the ladies, and you were to offer Brother Bao up to him, would that not be a fine thing?” Grandmother Jia laughed. “Even as sick as you are, girl Feng, your tongue is as sharp and clever as ever.” Just as the conversation was at its merriest, one of Lady Xing’s attendants came rushing in, crying at the top of her voice, “Old Mistress! Ladies! Something—something terrible has happened! A great horde of b-booted and capped b-bandits has come! They are overturning chests and cupboards and carrying things away!” Grandmother Jia and the others stared in stunned silence. Then they saw Pinger, her hair disheveled, leading Qiaojie in by the hand and weeping as she said, “Disaster! I was eating with the young mistress when Laiwang was brought in bound. He said, ‘Miss, send word inside at once and ask the ladies to withdraw. His Highness is about to enter and confiscate the family property.’ I panicked when I heard this and was about to go into my room for the important things, but a gang of men shoved and drove me out. We must quickly gather up the clothes and ornaments we need here.” On hearing this, Ladies Wang and Xing and the rest were frightened out of their wits and had no idea what to do. Xifeng alone had at first listened with her eyes wide open; then she suddenly reeled backward, fell to the floor, and lost consciousness. Before Grandmother Jia had heard the whole story, terror sent tears streaming from her eyes, and she could no longer utter a word. The whole room was now in an uproar, with people pulling at one person and tugging at another, when a succession of shouts rang out: “Tell the ladies inside to withdraw! His Highness is coming in!”

p.src: Poor Baochai, Baoyu, and the others were at their wits’ end. While the maids and old women on the floor were frantically lifting and pulling people about, Jia Lian came running in, panting for breath, and cried, “It is all right! It is all right! Thank heaven, His Highness has saved us!” They were just about to question him when Jia Lian saw Xifeng lying unconscious on the floor. He cried out wildly, then, fearing that the old lady too had been frightened into collapse, was nearly beside himself with anguish. Fortunately, Pinger managed to revive Xifeng and had someone support her. The old lady also recovered her senses, but her weeping left her breathless and faint, and she lay down on the kang. Li Wan comforted her again and again. Only then did Jia Lian compose himself and explain how the two princes had shown them mercy. Fearing that Grandmother Jia and Lady Xing might collapse again if they learned that Jia She had been arrested, he did not dare reveal it for the time being, and went out to see to matters in his own quarters.

p.src: As soon as he entered the room, he saw trunks forced open, cupboards smashed, and half their contents plundered. His eyes started with anguish; tears streamed down his face as he stood there dazed. Hearing someone call outside, he had no choice but to go out. There he found Jia Zheng and the officials registering the property, while one man reported, “One hundred and twenty-three articles of pure-gold jewelry, complete with pearls and precious stones. Thirteen strings of pearls; two pale-gold platters; two pairs of gold bowls; two gold handled bowls; forty gold spoons; eighty large silver bowls; twenty silver platters; two pairs of ivory chopsticks inlaid with gold in three places; four gilt ewers; three pairs of gilt slop basins; two tea saucers; seventy-six silver dishes; and thirty-six silver wine cups. Eighteen black fox pelts; six blue fox pelts; thirty-six sable pelts; thirty yellow fox pelts; twelve lynx pelts; three hemp-pattern pelts; sixty foreign gray pelts; forty gray fox-leg pelts; twenty dark-brown sheepskins; two raccoon pelts; two bundles of yellow fox-leg pelts; twenty pieces of white fox fur; thirty lengths of foreign woolen cloth; twenty-three lengths of serge; twelve lengths of velvet; ten tubular musk-rat furs; four square pieces of field-mouse fur; one roll of velvet; one square of spotted-deer hide; two tubular cloud-fox furs; one roll of young raccoon-dog fur; seven bundles of duck skin; one hundred and sixty gray squirrel pelts; eight badger pelts; six tiger skins; three seal skins; sixteen sea-otter skins; forty bundles of gray sheepskin; sixty-three black sheepskins; ten dark-fox hat brims; twelve Japanese-sable hat brims; two sable hat brims; sixteen small fox pelts; two river raccoon-dog pelts; two otter pelts; thirty-five cat skins; twelve lengths of Japanese cloth; one hundred and thirty rolls of silk and satin; one hundred and eighty-one rolls of gauze and damask; thirty-two rolls of feather-thread crepe; thirty rolls of Tibetan woolen cloth; eight rolls of figured python satin; three bundles of ramie cloth; three bundles of assorted cloth; one hundred and thirty-two fur garments of various kinds; and three hundred and forty cotton-padded, lined, unlined, gauze, and silk garments. Thirty-two jade ornaments; nine sets of belt fittings; more than five hundred objects of copper, pewter, and the like; eighteen clocks and watches; nine court necklaces; thirty-four figured python robes of various colors; three sets of imperial python-satin armrests and back cushions; eight sets of palace-style robes and skirts; one belt with a creamy-jade ring; and twelve rolls of yellow satin. Five thousand two hundred taels of standard silver, fifty taels of pure gold, and seven thousand strings of cash.” All the household utensils were gathered together, sealed, and registered; the imperial grant of the Rongguo residence was also itemized, while the title deeds to houses and land and the servants’ indentures were wrapped and sealed. Jia Lian listened furtively nearby, but when he heard no mention of his own possessions, he began to wonder why. Then he heard the two princes ask Jia Zheng, “Among the confiscated property are promissory notes that clearly show usurious lending. Who was responsible for it? You had better tell us the truth, Master Zheng.”

All the household utensils were gathered together, sealed, and registered; the imperial grant of the Rongguo residence was also itemized, while the title deeds to houses and land and the servants’ indentures were wrapped and sealed.
Jia Lian listened furtively nearby, but when he heard no mention of his own possessions, he began to wonder why.

u.src: Then he heard the two princes ask Jia Zheng, “Among the confiscated property are promissory notes that clearly show usurious lending. Who was responsible for it?
You had better tell us the truth, Master Zheng.”

p.src: At this, Jia Zheng knelt, knocked his head against the ground, and said, “In truth, this guilty official has taken no part in the management of the household and knows nothing whatever of these affairs. Only by questioning this guilty official’s nephew Jia Lian can the truth be learned.” Jia Lian hurried forward, knelt, and reported, “Since this chest of documents was found in your servant’s room, how could I dare claim ignorance of it? I beg Your Highnesses to show mercy; my uncle truly knew nothing about it.” The two princes said, “Your father has already been found guilty, so this can only be handled as part of the same case. It is only right that you should now admit to it. Have Jia Lian placed under guard, and let all the others disperse but remain within the residence. Master Zheng, you must take care and await the imperial decree. We are going into the palace to report to His Majesty; the officers and runners here will remain on guard.” With that, they entered their sedan chairs and departed through the gate. Jia Zheng and the others knelt at the inner gate to see them off. The Prince of Beijing extended a hand and said, “Do not worry.” His face showed deep reluctance to cause them pain.

p.src: Only then did Jia Zheng recover his wits, though he still stood there in a daze. Jia Lan said, “Grandfather, please go inside and see the Old Lady, then find some way to learn what has happened at the Eastern Mansion.” Jia Zheng hurriedly rose and went inside. At every doorway he saw women milling about in confusion, not knowing what to do. With no heart to question them, Jia Zheng went straight to Grandmother Jia’s room. Everyone there had a tear-stained face; Lady Wang, Baoyu, and the others stood around the old lady, weeping silently without a word. Lady Xing alone was overcome with convulsive sobbing. When they saw Jia Zheng enter, they all cried, “It is all right! It is all right!” Then they told the old lady, “The master has come back safe and sound. Please set your mind at ease.” Grandmother Jia, scarcely breathing, opened her eyes a little and said, “My son! I never thought I should see you again!” Before she had finished, she burst into loud sobs. At this, everyone in the room wept without cease. Fearing that such grief would harm his aged mother, Jia Zheng checked his own tears and said, “Please set your mind at ease, Mother. The affair is indeed a serious one, but through His Majesty’s heavenly grace and the kindness of the two princes, every possible consideration has been shown to us. Even the elder master has only been detained temporarily. Once the matter has been clarified, His Majesty will surely show him mercy as well. And now nothing more in our household is to be touched.” When Grandmother Jia saw that Jia She was not there, she grew sorrowful again, and only after Jia Zheng had comforted her repeatedly did she subside.

p.src: None of them dared disperse. Lady Xing alone returned to her own quarters, only to find every door sealed and the maids and old serving-women locked inside several rooms. With nowhere to go, Lady Xing burst into loud weeping and could only make her way to Xifeng’s quarters. She found seals pasted even upon the side rooms by the inner gate; only the main door stood open, and unceasing sobs came from within. Entering, Lady Xing saw Xifeng lying with her eyes closed, her face ashen as paper, while Ping’er wept quietly beside her. Lady Xing thought Xifeng was dead and began to weep again. Ping’er came forward to meet her and said, “Please do not cry, madam. When mistress was carried back, she seemed to be dead. Fortunately, after resting for a while she revived and wept a few times. Her breathing is now steady and the phlegm has subsided, so she is resting to calm herself. You too should try to compose yourself, madam. But I do not know how the Old Lady is faring.” Lady Xing made no reply but went back to Grandmother Jia’s quarters. Seeing only Jia Zheng’s people before her, while her own husband was detained, her daughter-in-law lay gravely ill, her daughter suffered hardship, and she herself had nowhere to call home, she could bear it no longer. Everyone tried to comfort her. Li Wan and the others had a room prepared for Lady Xing to occupy temporarily, while Lady Wang assigned servants to attend her.

p.src: Outside, Jia Zheng waited for the imperial decree with his heart pounding, stroking his beard and wringing his hands. He heard the soldiers on guard outside shouting in confusion, “Whose side are you on, anyway? Since you have fallen into our hands here, we shall enter you on our register. Tie him up and hand him over to the gentlemen of the Imperial Guard inside!” When Jia Zheng went out to look, he saw that it was Jiao Da and asked, “How did you come running here?” At this question, Jiao Da began wailing to heaven and stamping the earth. “Every day I warned those good-for-nothing masters, but they treated me as their enemy! Even you, sir, do not know what hardships I endured while following the Old Master! And now things have come to this! Master Zhen and young Rong were both seized and taken away by some prince or other; the bailiffs from some office dragged all the mistresses inside, their hair dishevelled, and thrust them together into an empty room, while those worthless dogs of men and women were penned up like swine and curs. Everything was seized and piled up; the wooden furnishings were smashed to pieces and the porcelain shattered to powder. They even tried to tie me up. I have lived eighty or ninety years, and only ever tied others up while following the Old Master—when have I ever let anyone tie me? I told them I belonged to the western mansion and ran out. But those men would not accept it and escorted me here, only for me to find the same thing happening here too. I care nothing for my life now. I may as well fight them to the death!” With that, he tried to dash his head against something. Seeing that he was old and mindful of the two princes’ orders, the bailiffs dared not treat him harshly. “Calm yourself, old sir,” they said. “This is being done by imperial command. Rest here for now, and wait until we hear what is to happen.” Jia Zheng now understood what had happened. Though he paid Jiao Da no further attention, his heart felt as if it were being twisted by a knife. “It is over, it is over!” he cried. Who could have imagined that our ruin would be so complete!” As he anxiously waited for news from inside, Xue Ke suddenly came running in, panting heavily. “I barely managed to get in! Where are you, Uncle?” “You have come at a good time,” said Jia Zheng, “but how did they let you in from outside?” “I pleaded with them again and again and promised them money,” replied Xue Ke. “That is why they allow me to come and go.” Jia Zheng told him about the confiscation and asked him to make inquiries. “Even close relatives would find it awkward to send word while the crisis is at its height, but you are well placed to pass messages.” Xue Ke said, “I never expected this to happen here. But I have already heard about the eastern mansion. It is finished.” “What crime have they actually committed?” asked Jia Zheng. Xue Ke replied, “Today, while making inquiries at the yamen about my elder brother’s sentence, I heard that two censors had received reports that Master Zhen enticed sons of distinguished families into gambling. That charge is still the lesser one. There is another, far graver charge: he forcibly took the wives and daughters of commoners as concubines, and when one of the women refused, he persecuted her until she died.

I fear even the Censorate may be found at fault, because that man Zhang had previously lodged a complaint there.” Before Jia Zheng had heard him out, he stamped his foot. “This is disastrous! It is all over, all over!” He heaved a sigh, and tears streamed down his face.

p.src: After offering a few words of comfort, Xue Ke went out again to seek information. Half a day later, he came back in and said, “Things look bad. I made inquiries at the Office of Scrutiny for Justice. I heard nothing about the two princes submitting their report to the throne, but I did hear that Censor Li impeached Ping'an Prefecture this morning on several grave counts: currying favor with officials in the capital, pandering to superiors, and oppressing the common people.” Jia Zheng cried anxiously, “Never mind other people’s affairs! What have you learned about us?” Xue Ke replied, “When they speak of Ping'an Prefecture, we are implicated too. The capital official named in the impeachment is Master She. He is accused of meddling in lawsuits for profit, so this only adds fuel to the fire. Even the officials who serve at court with him are scrambling to hide. Who would be willing to send us word? Even among the relatives and friends who just dispersed, some went straight home, while others stopped at a distance to await further news. Most hateful of all, those noble kinsmen were saying on the road, ‘Now the legacy left by our ancestors has brought disaster upon them. Who knows whose head it will fall upon next? Then the rest of us may have a chance to wield our authority.’” Before Jia Zheng had heard him out, he stamped his foot again. “It is all because our elder master is far too muddle-headed, and the eastern mansion has behaved far too disgracefully. We do not even know whether the Old Lady and Lian’s wife are alive or dead. Go and make further inquiries. I shall go and see the Old Lady. If there is any news, the sooner we learn of it, the better.” As he was speaking, a clamor arose inside: “The Old Lady has taken a turn for the worse!” In alarm, Jia Zheng hurried inside at once. Whether she lived or died will be revealed in the next chapter.
